atoms.text: Arthur wants to show you around the cities in England. Will you visit some cities with him?

instruction.text: Arthur wants to know if you recognise what English towns and cities look like. Select the three images of towns and cities in England.

feedback.end: Although London has a large population and many tall buildings, most other towns and cities in the UK are quite small and have a lot fewer people.
feedback.wrong: This is Hong Kong in Asia. England’s cities do not have as many huge skyscrapers.

instruction.text: Arthur asks if you know what you might find in English towns and cities. Drag the images to the correct words.
Arthur has marked a few of England’s biggest cities on his map. Find Birmingham on the map to visit it.
This is Birmingham. Find the red bus in the image to learn more.

feedback.end: Birmingham is England’s second biggest city after London. It is the city furthest away from the coast in the whole of the UK.

instruction.text: Find Leeds on the map to visit it.
This is Leeds. Find the tallest building in the image to learn more.

feedback.end: The world’s oldest running public railway is in Leeds. It was built in 1758 and still works today!

instruction.text: Find Bristol on the map to visit it.
This is Bristol. Find the bridge in the image to learn more.

feedback.end: Did you know? The world’s first ever bungee jump took place from this bridge!
